subject.title: Durable Core PR 4/6: persist agent-turn front doors

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this permanent cross-owner durable runtime, including the new `durable` configuration modes, shared SQLite evidence model, authority-mode fail-closed behavior, and restart no-replay policy?
rationale: The branch is a broad product and persistence architecture addition with intentional changes to fallback and recovery behavior; code review and contributor proof cannot choose the permanent core contract or its supported operational model.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded durable-core contract
options.body: Accept the direction, explicitly define the supported owners, config and migration guarantees, retention/inspection policy, and required fresh-install plus upgrade proof before merging the stack.

options.title: Keep lifecycle durability owner-specific
options.body: Decline the shared durable runtime and continue improving existing task, session, subagent, and delivery owners through narrow fixes or documented APIs.

options.title: Request a smaller proposal first
options.body: Pause implementation and ask for a maintainer-owned design that identifies the minimum missing core API before any new root config or shared durable schema lands.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded durable-core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the direction, explicitly define the supported owners, config and migration guarantees, retention/inspection policy, and required fresh-install plus upgrade proof before merging the stack.

likelyOwner.reason: This is the only concrete technical owner evidenced by the supplied feature history and can clarify the proposed boundary while a repository decision-maker sponsors or redirects it.
